Usage: place the lamp/burner in the heater slot, insert a wick, then put ethanol or vanilla alcohol in the fuel slot. Each bottle fills the lamp by purity (lamp capacity 500 ml). Click the lamp to toggle LOW 99°C / HIGH 160°C.
Wicks wear out while burning and are consumed when depleted; insert a new wick into the heating platform's wick slot to replace it.
Filtration bench: insert a liquid reagent plus filter paper. Paper filters by pore size and loses durability (destroyed when used up); each filtration raises the purify level by 1.
Usable as heating-platform fuel: put it in the fuel slot. Higher alcohol purity means stronger heat and slower consumption (lamp capacity 500 ml).

Gravity separation: put a liquid in and let it settle; layers collect in the output. No power, no filter paper, and purification level is unchanged. Beakers or flasks can be placed in an input slot and filled with reagents; two reagents may also react on direct contact. The note appears on the machine window note panel; if it is not shown there, the item tooltip also displays this usage text.

Pressure filtration: a liquid plus filter paper; paper traps contaminants by pore size and wears out, raising the purification level by 1 per pass. No power; has a dedicated filter-paper slot. Beakers or flasks can be placed in an input slot and filled with reagents; two reagents may also react on direct contact. The note appears on the machine window note panel; if it is not shown there, the item tooltip also displays this usage text.

Acid-base neutralisation: put an acid and a base in the two input slots to obtain brine plus water. No power required. Beakers or flasks can be placed in an input slot and filled with reagents; two reagents may also react on direct contact. The note appears on the machine window note panel; if it is not shown there, the item tooltip also displays this usage text.

Low-power evaporation: concentrate brine or ammonium nitrate solution into crystals, yielding a solid plus mother liquor. Needs a battery. Beakers or flasks can be placed in an input slot and filled with reagents; two reagents may also react on direct contact. The note appears on the machine window note panel; if it is not shown there, the item tooltip also displays this usage text.

Atmospheric synthesis: three input slots plus a module bay; reactions run at the temperature tier stated in the recipe. Needs a battery. Beakers or flasks can be placed in an input slot and filled with reagents; two reagents may also react on direct contact. The note appears on the machine window note panel; if it is not shown there, the item tooltip also displays this usage text.

Electrolysis: two input slots plus a module bay; direct current splits brine into gases and lye. Needs a battery (power 14). Beakers or flasks can be placed in an input slot and filled with reagents; two reagents may also react on direct contact. The note appears on the machine window note panel; if it is not shown there, the item tooltip also displays this usage text.

Heated gas generation: heat the input at the stated temperature tier to release gases such as Carbon Dioxide, Oxygen or ammonia. Needs a battery (power 6). Beakers or flasks can be placed in an input slot and filled with reagents; two reagents may also react on direct contact. The note appears on the machine window note panel; if it is not shown there, the item tooltip also displays this usage text.

Condensation and absorption: dissolve gases in water or condense them into liquids; inputs may include both liquid and gas. Needs a battery (power 8). Beakers or flasks can be placed in an input slot and filled with reagents; two reagents may also react on direct contact. The note appears on the machine window note panel; if it is not shown there, the item tooltip also displays this usage text.

Fractional distillation: collect different fractions by boiling point; three input slots. Needs a battery (power 12). Beakers or flasks can be placed in an input slot and filled with reagents; two reagents may also react on direct contact. The note appears on the machine window note panel; if it is not shown there, the item tooltip also displays this usage text.

High-pressure synthesis: three input slots; makes T3/T4 reagents under heat and pressure. Needs a battery (power 16). Beakers or flasks can be placed in an input slot and filled with reagents; two reagents may also react on direct contact. The note appears on the machine window note panel; if it is not shown there, the item tooltip also displays this usage text.

Gas filling: gas input plus a dedicated empty-canister/drum slot; produces industrial cylinders or drums according to gas purity. Needs a battery (power 9); this machine has no gas slots — feed gas items directly. Beakers or flasks can be placed in an input slot and filled with reagents; two reagents may also react on direct contact. The note appears on the machine window note panel; if it is not shown there, the item tooltip also displays this usage text.

Gas scrubbing: one gas input slot to wash out acidic/alkaline contaminants (gas only, no liquids). Needs a battery (power 7). Beakers or flasks can be placed in an input slot and filled with reagents; two reagents may also react on direct contact. The note appears on the machine window note panel; if it is not shown there, the item tooltip also displays this usage text.

Heating platform: the reaction slot accepts a vessel or a reagent directly; put the lamp/burner in the heater slot, a wick in the wick slot and ethanol or vanilla alcohol in the fuel slot; click the lamp to toggle LOW 99°C / HIGH 160°C; output appears on the right. Beakers or flasks can be placed in an input slot and filled with reagents; two reagents may also react on direct contact. The note appears on the machine window note panel; if it is not shown there, the item tooltip also displays this usage text.
